title.zh: 卷九十一 晉書17: 列傳六 房知溫 王建立 康福 安彥威 李周 張從訓 李繼忠 李頃 周光輔 符彥饒 羅周敬 鄭琮
title.en: Volume 91 Book of Later Jin 17: Biographies 6 - Fang Zhiwen, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, An Yanwei, Li Zhou, Zhang Congxun, Li Jizhong, Li Qing, Zhou Guangfu, Fu Yanrao, Luo Zhoujing, Zheng Cong
title.raw: 卷九十一 晉書17: 列傳六 房知溫 王建立 康福 安彥威 李周 張從訓 李繼忠 李頃 周光輔 符彥饒 羅周敬 鄭琮 Volume 91 Book of Later Jin 17: Biographies 6 - Fang Zhiwen, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, An Yanwei, Li Zhou, Zhang Congxun, Li Jizhong, Li Qing, Zhou Guangfu, Fu Yanrao, Luo Zhoujing, Zheng Cong

sentences.zh: 房知溫，字伯玉，兗州瑕丘人也。

translations.literal: Fang Zhiwen, styled Boyu, was a native of Xiaqiu in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhiwen, courtesy name Boyu, came from Xiaqiu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，籍名於本軍，為赤甲都官健。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength; his name was registered in the native army, and he served as an officer of the Red Armor company.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was strong and brave; enrolled in his home army, he became an officer in the Red Armor unit.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：知溫少年，與外弟徐某為盜於兗、鄆之境。）〉

translations.literal: (From Idle Talk of the Jade Hall: In his youth Zhiwen, together with a maternal cousin surnamed Xu, committed robbery in the borderlands of Yan and Yun.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Idle Talk of the Jade Hall records that in his youth Zhiwen and a maternal cousin, Xu, were bandits in the Yan and Yun region.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁將葛從周鎮其地，選置麾下。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Ge Congzhou garrisoned that region, he selected and placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang general Ge Congzhou was posted there, he took Zhiwen into his service.

sentences.zh: 時部將牛存節屯於鎮，好摴博，每求辨采者，知溫以善博見推，因得侍左右，遂熟於存節。

translations.literal: At that time the subordinate general Niu Cunjie was garrisoned at the post; fond of dice and wagering, whenever he sought someone to judge colors, Zhiwen was recommended for skill at gambling and thus gained attendance at his side, becoming acquainted with Cunjie.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Niu Cunjie was then stationed at the fort and loved gambling; when he needed someone to read the dice, Zhiwen's reputation for skill at the tables won him a place at Cunjie's side, and the two grew familiar.

sentences.zh: 及王師範遣劉鄩據兗州，梁祖命存節將兵討之，知溫夕縋出奔，存節喜而納焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Shifan sent Liu Yan to hold Yanzhou, the Liang founder ordered Cunjie to lead troops against him; Zhiwen let himself down by rope at night and fled out, and Cunjie gladly received him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan sent Liu Yan to seize Yanzhou, the Liang founder ordered Cunjie to attack; Zhiwen slipped out of the city by rope at night and fled to Cunjie, who welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 明夜，竊良馬一駟，復入城，鄩乃擢為裨將。

translations.literal: The next night he stole a team of four fine horses and re-entered the city; Yan then promoted him to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following night he stole a four-horse team and rode back into the city, whereupon Yan made him a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 鄩降，隸於同州劉知俊，知俊補為克和軍使。

translations.literal: When Yan surrendered, he came under Liu Zhijun of Tong Prefecture, who appointed him commander of the Kehe Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan surrendered, Zhiwen entered the service of Liu Zhijun at Tongzhou and was appointed commander of the Kehe Army.

sentences.zh: 知俊奔岐，改隸魏州楊師厚，以為馬步軍校，漸升至親隨指揮使，繼加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Zhijun fled to Qi, he was reassigned to Yang Shihou of Wei Prefecture and made a cavalry and infantry army officer; he rose gradually to personal escort commander and was later given the honorary title of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhijun fled to Qi, Zhiwen transferred to Yang Shihou at Weizhou as a cavalry and infantry officer, rose to commander of the personal guard, and was later made Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，賜姓，名紹英，改天雄軍馬步都指揮使，加檢校司徒、澶州刺史、行臺右千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, he was granted the imperial surname and given the name Shao Ying; he was made commander of cavalry and infantry of the Tianxiong Army, and further given the honorary titles of Acting Minister of Education, prefect of Chan Prefecture, and Grand General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards of the Field Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong took Wei, Zhiwen received the imperial surname and the name Shao Ying, was appointed commander of the Tianxiong cavalry and infantry, and was also made Honorary Minister of Education, prefect of Chanzhou, and Grand General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards on the field staff.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平梁，歷曹、貝州刺史，權充東北面蕃漢馬步都虞候，遣戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he served successively as prefect of Cao and Bei Prefectures, acted as overall deputy commander of barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry in the northeast, and was sent to garrison Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang was conquered, he served as prefect of Cao and Beizhou in turn, acted as deputy commander of barbarian and Han forces in the northeast, and was posted to garrison Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 明宗自鄴入洛，知溫與王晏球首赴焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong entered Luoyang from Ye, Zhiwen and Wang Yanqiu were the first to hurry to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong marched from Ye into Luoyang, Zhiwen and Wang Yanqiu were the first to come to his side.

sentences.zh: 明宗自總管府署知溫滑州兩使留後。

translations.literal: From his post as overall commander Mingzong appointed Zhiwen acting military governor of the two circuits of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While still overall commander, Mingzong appointed Zhiwen acting governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，授兗州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made military governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (926) he was appointed military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔充北面招討，屯於盧臺軍。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, an edict appointed him northern campaign commander, and he encamped at the Lutai Army post.
translations.idiomatic: On Mingzong's accession he was ordered to serve as northern campaign commander and encamped at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 以盧文進來歸，加特進、同平章事，賞招討之功也。

translations.literal: Because Lu Wenjin came over in submission, he was given the extraordinary rank of Grand Master and made Associate Grand Councillor, as a reward for his campaign achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wenjin defected to the court, Zhiwen was promoted to Grand Master and Associate Grand Councillor in reward for his work as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 後除烏震為招討副使，代知溫歸鎮。

translations.literal: Later Wu Zhen was appointed deputy campaign commander to replace Zhiwen and return him to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Zhen was made deputy campaign commander so that Zhiwen could return to his command.

sentences.zh: 知溫怒震遽至，有怨言，因縱博，誘牙兵殺震於席上。

translations.literal: Zhiwen was angry that Zhen had arrived so abruptly and nursed grievances; he therefore set up gambling and induced the garrison troops to kill Zhen at the gaming table.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by Zhen's sudden arrival, Zhiwen harbored resentment; he staged a gambling session and incited his garrison troops to kill Zhen at the table.

sentences.zh: 會次將安審通保騎軍隔河按甲不動，知溫懼不濟，乃束身渡水，復結審通，逐其亂軍以奏。

translations.literal: As it happened the deputy commander An Shentong held the cavalry across the river with arms at rest and did not move; fearing failure, Zhiwen bound himself and crossed the water, renewed ties with Shentong, and drove off the mutinous troops before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander An Shentong meanwhile held his cavalry on the far bank and would not advance; fearing the plot would fail, Zhiwen crossed the river in person, won Shentong over again, routed the mutineers, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷姑息知溫，下詔於鄴盡殺軍士家口老幼凡數萬，清漳為之變色。

translations.literal: At that time the court indulged Zhiwen; an edict ordered that at Ye all the families of the soldiers—old and young—be put to death, numbering tens of thousands in all, and the Clear Zhang River turned dark with blood.
translations.idiomatic: The court indulged Zhiwen; an edict had every soldier's dependents at Ye—old and young alike—slaughtered, tens of thousands in all, until the Zhang River ran dark with blood.

sentences.zh: 尋詔遣知溫就便之鎮，以安反側。

translations.literal: Soon an edict sent Zhiwen back to his convenient garrison post to settle unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered back to his post to calm the unrest.

sentences.zh: 俄改徐州節度使，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to military governor of Xu Prefecture and given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made military governor of Xuzhou and also appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷起兵伐高季興，授荊南招討使，知行府事。

translations.literal: When the court raised troops against Gao Jixing, he was made campaign commander of Jingnan and acted as administrator of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched against Gao Jixing, he was appointed Jingnan campaign commander and placed in charge of headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，起復雲麾將軍，墨缞即戎，竟無功而還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; recalled from mourning as General of the Cloud-Banner Guards, he took the field in unbleached hemp and in the end returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his mother; recalled as General of the Cloud-Banner Guards, he took command in mourning dress but achieved nothing and returned.

sentences.zh: 長興中，節制文陽。

translations.literal: During Changxing he controlled Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era (930–933) he held authority over Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 越二年，除平盧軍節度使，累官至開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼中書令，封東平王，食邑五千戶，食實封三百戶。

translations.literal: Two years later he was made military governor of the Pinglu Army; he rose in office to Grand Preceptor with the rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Acting Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with a fief of five thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became military governor of Pinglu; he eventually reached Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with a nominal fief of five thousand households and three hundred actual.

sentences.zh: 天福元年冬十二月辛巳，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month of winter in the first year of Tianfu he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the twelfth month of the first Tianfu year (936) he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，歸葬於瑕丘，詔立神道碑。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; his remains were returned for burial at Xiaqiu, and an edict ordered a spirit-way stele erected.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, buried at Xiaqiu, and the court ordered a spirit-way stele set up for him.

sentences.zh: 知溫性粗獷，動罕由禮。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's nature was coarse and rough; his actions rarely followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen was coarse by nature and seldom observed propriety.

sentences.zh: 每迎待王人，不改戎服，寡言笑，多縱左右排辱賓僚，他日知誤，亦無愧色。

translations.literal: Whenever he received imperial envoys he did not change out of military dress, spoke little and laughed little, and often let his attendants insult and humiliate his staff; when he later knew he had erred, he still showed no shame.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving imperial envoys he kept his military dress, spoke little, and often let his men bully his staff; even when he later realized his mistake, he showed no shame.

sentences.zh: 始與唐末帝嘗失意於杯盤間，以白刃相恐，及末帝即位，知溫憂甚，末帝乃封王爵以寧之也。

translations.literal: Earlier he and the Last Tang Emperor had once quarreled over cups and dishes and threatened each other with bare blades; when the Last Emperor took the throne Zhiwen was deeply afraid, and the Last Emperor therefore enfeoffed him with a princely title to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: He and the Last Tang Emperor had once quarreled at table and drawn blades on each other; when the emperor acceded, Zhiwen was terrified, so the emperor enfeoffed him as a prince to put his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 知溫徑赴洛陽，申其宿過，且感新恩，末帝開懷以厚禮慰而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhiwen went straight to Luoyang, confessed his old offense, and also expressed gratitude for the new favor; the Last Emperor opened his heart, comforted him with generous gifts, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen went directly to Luoyang, confessed his past offense, and thanked the emperor for his grace; the Last Emperor received him warmly, honored him generously, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 及還郡，厚斂不已，積貨數百萬，治第於南城，出則以妓樂相隨，任意所之，曾不以政事為務。

translations.literal: When he returned to his command he levied heavy taxes without cease, amassed goods worth millions, built a mansion in the southern city, and whenever he went out was followed by singing girls and musicians, going wherever he pleased and never taking administration as his business.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his province he taxed relentlessly, amassed millions in goods, built a mansion in the southern quarter, and went abroad with musicians and courtesans wherever he pleased, caring nothing for government.

sentences.zh: 有幕客顏衎者，正直之士也，委曲陳其利病，知溫不能用焉。

translations.literal: He had a staff adviser named Yan Kan, an upright man, who tactfully set forth the advantages and harms, but Zhiwen could not employ his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Yan Kan was an upright man who tactfully explained what would help and what would harm him, but Zhiwen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義入洛，尚不即進獻，耀兵於牙帳之下，衎正色謂曰：「清泰富有天下，多力善戰，豈明公之比！

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor raised the righteous cause and entered Luoyang, he still did not immediately submit tribute but displayed troops beneath his headquarters tent; Yan said sternly to him: "Qingtai possesses the realm and is strong and skilled in war—how can he be compared with you!
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched into Luoyang on his righteous campaign, Zhiwen still delayed his submission and paraded troops before his headquarters; Yan said sternly, "Qingtai holds the empire, is powerful, and fights well—how can you compare with him!

sentences.zh: 而天運有歸，坐成灰燼。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's mandate has its destination, and sitting still one becomes ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's mandate has already shifted, and those who sit idle will be reduced to ashes.

sentences.zh: 今青州遷延不貢，何以求安？

translations.literal: Now Qing Prefecture delays and does not offer tribute—how can you seek security?
translations.idiomatic: If Qingzhou now delays its tribute, how will you keep yourself safe?

sentences.zh: 千百武夫，無足為恃，深為大王之所憂也。

translations.literal: A thousand or ten thousand fighting men are not worth relying on—this is what Your Highness should deeply worry about.
translations.idiomatic: A few thousand soldiers are no real support—that is what should truly worry you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」知溫遂馳表稱賀，青人乃安。

translations.literal: " Zhiwen then hurried a memorial of congratulation, and the people of Qing were thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhiwen then sent a congratulatory memorial at once, and the people of Qingzhou were reassured.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以沈湎成疾而卒，部曲將吏分其所聚，例為富室。

translations.literal: Before long, through deep drinking he fell ill and died; the officers and clerks of his command divided what he had amassed and in every case became wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill from dissipation and died; his officers divided his hoard and each became a rich family in turn.

sentences.zh: 衎又勸其子彥儒進錢十萬貫，以助國用，朝廷除彥儒為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan also urged his son Yanru to present one hundred thousand strings of cash to aid state expenses; the court appointed Yanru prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also persuaded his son Yanru to present one hundred thousand strings of cash to aid the treasury; the court then appointed Yanru prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其家幸獲保全，皆衎之力也。

translations.literal: His family was fortunate to be preserved intact—all through Yan's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: The family was spared—entirely through Yan's doing.

sentences.zh: 王建立，遼州榆社人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jianli was a native of Yushe in Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianli came from Yushe in Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秋，祖嘉，父弁，累贈太保。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Qiu, his grandfather Jia, and his father Bian; all were posthumously given the title of Grand Guardian in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qiu, grandfather Jia, and father Bian were each posthumously honored as Grand Guardian in turn.

sentences.zh: 建立少鷙猛無檢。

translations.literal: Jianli in youth was fierce and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jianli was fierce and undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 明宗領代州刺史，擢為虞候將。

translations.literal: When Mingzong held the post of prefect of Dai Prefecture, he promoted him to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was prefect of Daizhou, he promoted Jianli to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 莊宗鎮晉陽，以諸陵在代郡，遣女使饗祭，其下有擾於民者，建立必捕而笞之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was stationed at Jinyang, because the imperial tombs were in Dai Commandery he sent palace women to offer sacrifices; whenever subordinates disturbed the people, Jianli always seized and flogged them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was at Jinyang, palace women were sent to sacrifice at the tombs in Dai; whenever attendants harassed the people, Jianli arrested and flogged them.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，令收之，為明宗所護而免，由是知名。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry and ordered him seized; Mingzong protected him and he was spared, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was furious and ordered his arrest, but Mingzong shielded him and he was spared; from then on his name was known.

sentences.zh: 明宗歷遷藩鎮，皆署為牙門都校，累奏加檢校司空。

translations.literal: As Mingzong moved through successive frontier commands, he always appointed him chief of the headquarters guard, and repeatedly memorialized to add the honorary title of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mingzong was transferred to a new command, he made Jianli chief of headquarters guards, and repeatedly had him promoted to Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為魏軍所迫，時皇后曹氏、淑妃王氏在常山，使建立殺其監護並部下兵，故明宗家屬因而保全。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was pressed by the Wei army, the empress Cao and the honored consort Wang were at Changshan; he had Jianli kill their guards and the troops under them, and thus Mingzong's family was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was driven by the Wei army, Empress Cao and Honored Consort Wang were at Changshan; Jianli killed their guards and escort troops, and Mingzong's family was thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以功授鎮州節度副使，加檢校司徒，旋為留後。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, for his merit Jianli was made deputy military governor of Zhen Prefecture and given the honorary title of Acting Minister of Education; shortly he became acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Mingzong rewarded him with the deputy governorship of Zhenzhou and the honorary title Minister of Education, and soon made him acting governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，正授節旄，繼加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he received the full commission as military governor, and was then given the honorary titles of Acting Grand Commandant and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the full commission as military governor, then Honorary Grand Commandant and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 會王都據中山叛，密使通弟兄之好。

translations.literal: When Wang Du held Zhongshan in rebellion, secret envoys were exchanged to pledge brotherly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du rebelled from Zhongshan, the two exchanged secret envoys pledging brotherhood.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：王都陰與謀復河北故事，建立陽許而密奏之。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: Wang Du secretly plotted with him to restore the old Hebei arrangement; Jianli agreed openly but reported it in secret.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Wang Du secretly plotted to restore the old Hebei arrangement; Jianli agreed in public but reported him in secret.)〉

sentences.zh: 安重誨素與建立不協，知其事，奏之。

translations.literal: An Chonghui had long been at odds with Jianli; learning of the affair, he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui, who had long been at odds with Jianli, learned of the matter and reported it.

sentences.zh: 明宗慮陷建立，尋征赴闕，

translations.literal: Mingzong feared Jianli would be trapped, and soon summoned him to court,
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong feared Jianli would be framed and soon summoned him to court,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：建立奏重誨專權，求入朝面言其狀，帝召之。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: Jianli memorialized that Chonghui monopolized power and asked to enter court to state the case in person; the emperor summoned him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Jianli reported that Chonghui was monopolizing power and asked to come to court to speak in person; the emperor summoned him.)〉

sentences.zh: 拜右僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、判鹽鐵戶部度支，充集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and controller of the Salt and Iron Commission, Ministry of Revenue, and Directorate of Budget, and made Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director, concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, controller of salt, iron, revenue, and budget affairs, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 天成四年，出為青州節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng he was sent out as military governor of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancheng (929) he was made military governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，移鎮上黨，辭不赴任，請退居丘園，制以太子少保致仕，建立自是郁郁不得志。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to garrison Shangdang; he declined to take up the post and asked to retire to field and garden; by decree he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired, and from then on Jianli was depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Shangdang but refused the post and asked to retire; he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and left office, and from then on lived in frustration.

sentences.zh: 長興中，嘗欲求見，中旨不許，皆重誨蔽之也。

translations.literal: During Changxing he once sought an audience, but the imperial order did not permit it—all because Chonghui concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he once sought an audience, but the court refused—Chonghui had blocked him.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，末帝召赴闕，授天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai the Last Emperor summoned him to court and made him military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai the Last Emperor summoned him to court and appointed him military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 建立少歷軍校，職當捕盜，及位居方伯，為政嚴烈。

translations.literal: Jianli in youth had served as an army officer whose duty was to catch bandits; when he reached the rank of regional lord his government was severe and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli had begun as an army officer charged with catching bandits; once he became a regional governor his rule was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 閭裏有惡跡者，必族而誅之，其刑失於入者，不可勝紀，故當時人目之為「王垛疊」，言殺其人而積其屍也。

translations.literal: Whenever there was evil conduct in the villages he always exterminated the whole clan; cases in which punishment was excessive beyond what was warranted cannot be counted, and therefore people of the time called him "Wang the Corpse-Stacker," meaning that he killed people and piled up their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone with a criminal record in the villages he exterminated to the last of the clan; wrongful executions were beyond count, and people nicknamed him "Wang the Corpse-Stacker" for piling up the dead.

sentences.zh: 後聞末帝失勢，殺副使李彥赟及從事一人，報其私怨，人甚鄙之。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that the Last Emperor had lost power, he killed the deputy commissioner Li Yanyun and one staff member to settle private grievances; people despised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on hearing that the Last Emperor had fallen, he killed deputy commissioner Li Yanyun and a staff member to settle old scores, and people despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，再為青州節度使，累加檢校太尉、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he again became military governor of Qing Prefecture and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu acceded, Jianli again became military governor of Qingzhou and was eventually made Honorary Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建立晚年，歸心釋氏，飯僧營寺，戒殺慎獄，民稍安之。

translations.literal: In his later years Jianli turned his heart to Buddhism, fed monks and built temples, forbade killing and was cautious in prisons, and the people were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to Buddhism, fed monks and built temples, forbade killing and eased punishments, and the people were somewhat relieved.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，封臨淄王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Tianfu year (937) he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 明年，封東平王。

translations.literal: The next year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 五年，入覲，高祖曰：「三紀前老兄，宜賜不拜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he came to court for an audience; the High Ancestor said: "An elder brother from three reigns ago should be granted exemption from bowing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (940) he came to court; Gaozu said, "An old comrade from three reigns ago should be excused from bowing.

sentences.zh: 」仍許肩輿入朝，上殿則使二宦者掖之，論者榮之。

translations.literal: " He also permitted him to enter court in a shoulder-carried litter, and when he ascended the hall had two eunuchs support him; commentators regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: " He also allowed him to attend in a litter, and when he entered the hall two eunuchs supported him—a mark of honor, people said.

sentences.zh: 尋表乞休致，高祖不允。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to retire; the High Ancestor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire, but Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 乃授潞州節度使，割遼、沁二州為上黨屬郡，加檢校太師，進封韓王，以光其故裏。

translations.literal: He was then made military governor of Lu Prefecture; Liao and Qin Prefectures were carved out as subordinate commanderies of Shangdang; he was given the honorary title of Acting Grand Preceptor and advanced to Prince of Han to glorify his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed military governor of Luzhou; Liaozhou and Qinzhou were detached as subordinate prefectures of Shangdang; he was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and advanced to Prince of Han to honor his homeland.

sentences.zh: 至鎮逾月而疾作，有大星墜於府署，建立即召賓介竺嶽草遺章，又謂其子守恩曰：「榆社之地，桑梓存焉，桑以養生，梓以送死。

translations.literal: More than a month after reaching his post illness set in; a great star fell within the government compound; Jianli at once summoned his staff adviser Zhu Yue to draft his final memorial, and also said to his son Shou'en: "At Yushe in Yushe Commandery our native place remains; mulberry nourishes life, catalpa sees one to the grave.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month after reaching his post he fell ill; a great star fell in his compound; Jianli summoned his adviser Zhu Yue to draft his final instructions and told his son Shou'en, "In Yushe our homeland still stands—mulberry feeds the living, catalpa carries the dead.

sentences.zh: 余生為壽宮，刻銘石室，死當速葬，葬必從儉，違吾是言，非孝也。

translations.literal: In life I have built a longevity palace and carved inscriptions in a stone chamber; when dead I should be buried quickly, and burial must be frugal—whoever violates these words of mine is unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: In life I have built my tomb and carved my epitaph; when I die bury me quickly and keep the rites simple—whoever disobeys these words is no true son.

sentences.zh: 」旋以病篤而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward his illness became grave and he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon his illness worsened and he died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 冊贈尚書令。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建立先人之墳在於榆社，其崗阜重復，松檜藹然，占者云「後必出公侯」，故建立自為墓，恐子孫易之也。

translations.literal: The tombs of Jianli's forebears were at Yushe; the hills rose in layers and pines and cypresses were lush; diviners said "later there will surely come dukes and marquises," and therefore Jianli built his own tomb himself, fearing his descendants might change it.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were buried at Yushe on layered hills thick with pine and cypress; diviners said nobles would spring from the line, so Jianli built his own tomb lest descendants alter the site.

sentences.zh: 子守恩，《周書》有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shou'en has a biography in the Book of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou'en has a biography in the Zhou History.

sentences.zh: 康福，蔚州人，世為本州軍校。

translations.literal: Kang Fu was a native of Wei Prefecture; for generations his family had been army officers of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu came from Weizhou; for generations his family had served as army officers there.

sentences.zh: 祖嗣，蕃漢都知兵馬使，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His grandfather Si was overall commander of barbarian and Han forces and was posthumously given the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Si had been overall commander of barbarian and Han forces and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父公政，歷職至平塞軍使，累贈太傅。

translations.literal: His father Gongzheng rose through offices to commander of the Pingsai Army and was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongzheng rose to commander of the Pingsai Army and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 福便弓馬，少事後唐武皇，累補軍職，充承天軍都監。

translations.literal: Fu was skilled with bow and horse; in youth he served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang and was repeatedly appointed to army posts, serving as overall supervisor of the Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled with bow and horse, he served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang in youth, rose through army posts, and became overall supervisor of the Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，嘗謂左右曰：「我本蕃人，以羊馬為活業。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne he once said to those beside him: "I am originally a barbarian; my livelihood is sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded he once told his attendants, "I am a barbarian by origin; sheep and horses are my livelihood.

sentences.zh: 彼康福者，體貌豐厚，宜領財貨，可令總轄馬牧。

translations.literal: That Kang Fu has a full and substantial physique and is fit to oversee goods and wealth; he may be ordered to take overall charge of horse pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: That Kang Fu is stout and solid—fit to manage wealth; put him in charge of the horse herds.

sentences.zh: 」由是署為馬坊使，大有蕃息。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was appointed horse-pasture commissioner, and the herds greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore made horse-pasture commissioner, and the herds flourished.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為亂兵所迫，將離魏縣，會福牧小坊馬數千匹於相州，乃驅而歸。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was pressed by mutinous troops and was about to leave Wei County, it happened that Fu was pasturing several thousand horses of the minor pastures at Xiang Prefecture; he drove them back in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was driven by mutineers and about to leave Wei County, Fu happened to be pasturing several thousand horses at Xiangzhou and drove them back to him.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，授飛龍使，俄轉磁州刺史，充襄州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Fu was made commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guards; shortly he was transferred to prefect of Ci Prefecture and made overall supervisor of Xiang Prefecture's cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On Mingzong's accession he was made commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guards, soon transferred to prefect of Cizhou, and placed in charge of Xiangzhou's forces.

sentences.zh: 尋以江陵叛命，朝廷舉兵伐之，以福為荊南道行營兵馬都監，俄以王師無功而還。

translations.literal: Soon, because Jiangling defied orders, the court raised troops against it and made Fu overall supervisor of cavalry and infantry for the Jingnan campaign headquarters; shortly the imperial army returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling rebelled the court marched against it and made Fu overall supervisor of the Jingnan campaign force, but the imperial army soon withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 福善諸蕃語，明宗視政之暇，每召入便殿，諮訪時之利病，福即以蕃語奏之。

translations.literal: Fu was skilled in various barbarian languages; in Mingzong's leisure from attending to government he was often summoned to the private hall to be consulted on the advantages and harms of the times, and Fu would report in barbarian speech.
translations.idiomatic: Fu knew several barbarian languages; in his leisure from government Mingzong often summoned him to the private hall to ask about current affairs, and Fu answered in barbarian speech.

sentences.zh: 樞密使重誨惡焉，常面戒之曰：「康福但亂奏事，有日斬之！

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chonghui hated this and often warned him to his face: "Kang Fu only muddles reports to the throne—one day he will be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner An Chonghui hated this and often warned him to his face, "Kang Fu only muddles what he reports to the throne—one day I'll have his head!

sentences.zh: 」福懼。

translations.literal: " Fu was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu was terrified.

sentences.zh: 會靈武兵馬留後韓潯，以人情不協，慮為所圖，上表請帥，制加福光祿大夫、檢校司空，行涼州刺史，充朔方、河西等軍節度，靈威雄警甘肅等州觀察處置、管內營田、押蕃落、溫池榷稅等使。

translations.literal: As it happened Han Xun, acting commander of Lingwu's cavalry and infantry, because local sentiment was not harmonious feared he would be plotted against and memorialized requesting a commander-in-chief; by decree Fu was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Works, acting prefect of Liang Prefecture, and military governor of the Shuofang and Hexi armies, with authority as observer and administrator of Ling, Wei, Xiong, Jing, Gan, and Su Prefectures, director of garrison farming within the circuit, commissioner for restraining barbarian tribes, and commissioner for the monopoly tax at Wench Pool.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xun, acting commander at Lingwu, feared conspiracy because local sentiment was against him and asked for a new commander, Fu was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Minister of Works, acting prefect of Liangzhou, military governor of Shuofang and Hexi, observer of Ling, Wei, Xiong, Jing, Gan, and Su, with authority over garrison farming, barbarian tribes, and the Wench Pool monopoly.

sentences.zh: 福之是拜，蓋重誨嫉而出之，福泣而辭之。

translations.literal: Fu's receiving this appointment was because Chonghui, jealous, had him sent out; Fu wept as he took leave.
translations.idiomatic: This appointment was Chonghui's way of banishing a rival; Fu wept as he took leave.

sentences.zh: 明宗宣重誨別與商議，重誨奏曰：「臣累奉聖旨，令與康福一事，今福驟升節鎮，更欲何求！

translations.literal: Mingzong summoned Chonghui to discuss separately; Chonghui reported: "Your servant has repeatedly received the sacred command to settle one matter with Kang Fu; now Fu has suddenly risen to a frontier command—what more does he seek!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong summoned Chonghui to discuss the matter separately; Chonghui said, "I have repeatedly been ordered to settle affairs with Kang Fu; he has now been made a frontier commander overnight—what more could he want!

sentences.zh: 況已有成命，難於改移。

translations.literal: Moreover there is already a completed order, and it is hard to change.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the appointment has already been issued and cannot easily be reversed.

sentences.zh: 」明宗不得已，謂福曰：「重誨不肯，非朕意也。

translations.literal: " Mingzong had no choice and said to Fu: "Chonghui will not agree—this is not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong had no choice and told Fu, "Chonghui will not budge—this is not what I wanted.

sentences.zh: 」福辭，明宗曰：「朕遣兵援助，勿過憂也。

translations.literal: " Fu took leave; Mingzong said: "I will send troops to aid you—do not worry overly.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu took his leave. Mingzong said, "I will send troops to support you—do not worry too much.

sentences.zh: 」因令將軍牛知柔領兵送赴鎮。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the general Niu Zhirou to lead troops escorting him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered General Niu Zhirou to escort him to his post with troops.

sentences.zh: 行次青崗峽，會大雪，令人登山望之，見川下煙火，吐蕃數千帳在焉，寇不之覺，因分軍三道以掩之。

translations.literal: Marching to Qinggang Gorge they encountered heavy snow; men were sent up the mountain to look out and saw smoke and fires below in the valley—several thousand Tibetan tents were there; the enemy did not notice them, and therefore the army was divided into three routes to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinggang Gorge they met heavy snow; scouts climbed the heights and saw smoke below—thousands of Tibetan tents, the enemy unaware. Fu split his force into three columns and fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 蕃眾大駭，棄帳幕而走，殺之殆盡，獲玉璞、羊馬甚多。

translations.literal: The barbarian masses were greatly terrified, abandoned their tents and fled, and were nearly all killed; many jade disks, sheep, and horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans fled in panic, abandoning their tents; nearly all were killed, and great quantities of jade, sheep, and horses were taken.

sentences.zh: 到鎮歲餘，西戎皆款附，改賜福耀忠匡定保節功臣，累加官爵。

translations.literal: More than a year after reaching his post, the western barbarians all came in sincere submission; Fu was given the title of Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty in Rectifying and Securing the Frontier, and offices and ranks were repeatedly added.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year of taking his post the western tribes all submitted; he was given the title Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty in Securing the Frontier and received repeated promotions.

sentences.zh: 福鎮靈武凡三歲，每歲大稔，倉儲盈羨，有馬千駟，因為人所譖。

translations.literal: Fu governed Lingwu for three years in all; every year there was a great harvest, granaries overflowed, and he had a thousand teams of horses, and therefore people slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu governed Lingwu for three years; harvests were abundant every year, granaries overflowed, and he kept a thousand horse teams—so people slandered him.

sentences.zh: 安重誨奏曰：「累據使臣所言，康福大有寶貨，必負朝廷。

translations.literal: An Chonghui reported: "According repeatedly to what envoys have said, Kang Fu has great stores of treasure and goods and must be disloyal to the court.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui reported, "Envoys repeatedly say Kang Fu has vast treasure and must be disloyal to the court.

sentences.zh: 」明宗密遣人謂曰：「朕何負於卿，而有異心耶！

translations.literal: " Mingzong secretly sent someone to say to him: "What have I done against you, that you should have a different heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong secretly sent word: "What have I done to you that you would turn against me!

sentences.zh: 」福奏曰：「臣受國重恩，有死無貳，豈願負於聖人，此必讒人之言也。

translations.literal: " Fu reported: "Your servant has received the state's heavy grace; I would die rather than be double-minded—how could I wish to be disloyal to the Sage? This must be the words of slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu replied, "I owe the state a great debt and would die before being disloyal—this must be slander.

sentences.zh: 」因表乞入覲，不允。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized asking to enter court for an audience, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized asking to come to court, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 及再上章，隨而赴闕，移授彰義軍節度使，又轉邠州，檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When he memorialized again, he followed and went to court; he was transferred to military governor of the Zhangyi Army, then transferred to Bin Prefecture as Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When he memorialized again he went to court and was transferred to military governor of Zhangyi, then to Binzhou as Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，移鎮秦州，加特進、開國侯，充西面都部署。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was transferred to garrison Qin Prefecture, given the extraordinary rank of Grand Master and made Marquis with a state-founding fief, and made overall western deployment commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was transferred to Qinzhou, made Grand Master and Marquis, and appointed overall western deployment commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，就加檢校太尉、開國公。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor received the Mandate, Fu was at once given the honorary title of Acting Grand Commandant and made Duke with a state-founding fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Fu was at once made Honorary Grand Commandant and Duke.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又加同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was also made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 及移領河中，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to lead Hezhong, he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When he took command of Hezhong he was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以天和節入覲，改賜輸忠守正翊亮功臣，加開府儀同三司，增食邑至五千戶，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: On the Tianhe festival he came to court for an audience; he was given the title of Meritorious Minister for Loyal Submission, Upright Guardianship, and Assisting Brilliance, made Grand Preceptor with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and his fief was increased to five thousand households with an actual enfeoffment of five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tianhe festival he came to court and was given the title Meritorious Minister for Loyal Submission and Upright Service, made Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, with a nominal fief of five thousand households and five hundred actual.

sentences.zh: 久之，受代歸闕。

translations.literal: After a long time he was relieved and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was relieved and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於京師，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in the capital, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh Tianfu year (942) he died in the capital at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚曰武安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Martial Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Martial Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 福無軍功，屬明宗龍躍，有際會之幸，擢自小校，暴為貴人，每食非羊之全髀不能飫腹，與士大夫交言，懵無所別。

translations.literal: Fu had no military merit; it happened that when Mingzong rose like a dragon he had the good fortune of timely opportunity, was promoted from a petty officer, and suddenly became a noble; at each meal he could not fill his belly unless he had a whole sheep's hindquarter, and when conversing with scholar-officials he was muddled and could distinguish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had no military merit; when Mingzong rose to power he had the luck to be in the right place, vaulted from petty officer to grandee, ate only whole sheep haunches at a sitting, and could barely tell one scholar-official from another in conversation.

sentences.zh: 在天水日，嘗有疾，幕客謁問，福擁衾而坐。

translations.literal: While at Tianshui he once fell ill; staff guests came to inquire after him, and Fu sat wrapped in his quilt.
translations.idiomatic: While at Tianshui he once fell ill; when staff came to call, he sat wrapped in his quilt.

sentences.zh: 客有退者，謂同列曰：「錦衾爛兮！

translations.literal: One guest who withdrew said to his colleagues: "What a splendid brocade quilt!
translations.idiomatic: One guest who had left said to his colleagues, "What a splendid brocade quilt!

sentences.zh: 」福聞之，遽召言者，怒視曰：「吾雖生於塞下，乃唐人也，何得以為爛奚！

translations.literal: " Fu heard it, hurriedly summoned the speaker, glared angrily and said: "Although I was born beyond the passes, I am a man of Tang—how dare you call me a splendid barbarian!
translations.idiomatic: " Fu heard this, summoned the man, and glared: "I was born beyond the passes, but I am a Tang man—how dare you call me a splendid barbarian!

sentences.zh: 」因叱出之，由是諸客不敢措辭。

translations.literal: " He therefore shouted and drove him out; from then on the guests did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him thrown out, and from then on no guest dared speak freely.

sentences.zh: 復有末客姓駱，其先與後唐懿祖來自金山府，因公宴，福謂從事輩曰：「駱評事官則卑，門族甚高，真沙陀也。

translations.literal: There was also a junior guest surnamed Luo whose forebears had come from Jinshan Prefecture with the August Ancestor of Later Tang; at a public banquet Fu said to his staff: "Reviewer Luo's office is low, but his clan is very eminent—a true Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a junior guest named Luo whose ancestors had come from Jinshan with Later Tang's August Ancestor; at a banquet Fu told his staff, "Reviewer Luo's rank is low, but his clan is eminent—a true Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 」聞者竊笑焉。

translations.literal: " Those who heard secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard smiled to themselves.

sentences.zh: 子三人：長曰延沼，歷隨、澤二州刺史；

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest was named Yanzhao and served successively as prefect of Sui and Ze Prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest, Yanzhao, served as prefect of Suizhou and Zezhou;

sentences.zh: 次曰延澤、延壽，俱歷內職焉。

translations.literal: the next were Yanze and Yanshou, both of whom held inner-court posts.
translations.idiomatic: the next two, Yanze and Yanshou, both held posts at court.

sentences.zh: 安彥威，字國俊，代州崞縣人。

translations.literal: An Yanwei, styled Guojun, was a native of Guo County in Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Yanwei, courtesy name Guojun, came from Guo County in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 少時以軍卒隸唐明宗麾下，彥威善射，頗知兵法，明宗愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a soldier under Tang Emperor Mingzong; Yanwei was skilled at archery and knew military strategy well; Mingzong favored him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served as a soldier under Mingzong; skilled at archery and versed in strategy, he won Mingzong's favor.

sentences.zh: 及領諸鎮節鉞，彥威常為牙將，以謹厚見信。

translations.literal: When he led the military commissions of various commands, Yanwei was often a headquarters officer and was trusted for his prudence and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mingzong held a frontier command, Yanwei served as a headquarters officer and was trusted for his steadiness.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，皇子從榮鎮鄴，彥威為護聖指揮使；

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered and established rule, the prince Congrong was stationed at Ye and Yanwei was commander of the Imperial Guard;
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Prince Congrong was posted at Ye and Yanwei became commander of the Imperial Guard;

sentences.zh: 以從榮判六軍，彥威入司禁衛，遙領鎮州節度使。

translations.literal: when Congrong was put in charge of the Six Armies, Yanwei entered to administer the palace guards and held the military governorship of Zhen Prefecture in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: when Congrong was placed over the Six Armies, Yanwei took charge of the palace guards and held the Zhenzhou governorship in absentia.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入立，拜彥威北京留守，徙鎮歸德，是時河決滑州，命彥威塞之，彥威出私錢募民治堤。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered and established rule, Yanwei was made northern capital regent, then transferred to garrison Guide; at that time the Yellow River burst its banks at Hua Prefecture and he was ordered to block it; Yanwei spent his private funds to recruit the people to repair the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Yanwei was made regent of the northern capital, then transferred to Guide; when the Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou he was ordered to stem the flood and spent his own money to hire labor for the dikes.

sentences.zh: 遷西京留守，遭歲大饑，彥威賑饑民，民有犯法，皆寬貸之，饑民愛之不忍去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to western capital regent; a year of great famine struck; Yanwei relieved the starving people, and whenever the people violated the law he pardoned them all; the starving people loved him and could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to regent of the western capital, he met a great famine; he fed the hungry, pardoned offenders, and the people loved him so much they would not leave.

sentences.zh: 旋丁母艱，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: Shortly he entered mourning for his mother, his grief and devastation exceeding the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his mother, grieving beyond the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 少帝與契丹構患，拜彥威北面行營副都統，彥威悉以家財佐軍，後以疾卒於京師。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor had trouble with the Khitan, Yanwei was made deputy overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Yanwei devoted all his family wealth to aid the army, and later died of illness in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor clashed with the Khitan, Yanwei was made deputy commander of the northern campaign; he spent his entire family fortune on the army and later died of illness in the capital.

sentences.zh: 彥威與太妃同宗，少帝事以為舅，彥威未嘗以為言。

translations.literal: Yanwei was of the same clan as the Honored Consort; the Young Emperor treated him as a maternal uncle, but Yanwei never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was kin to the Honored Consort; the Young Emperor treated him as an uncle, but Yanwei never mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 及卒，太妃臨哭，人始知其為國戚，當時益重其人焉。

translations.literal: When he died the Honored Consort came in person to mourn; only then did people know he was an imperial relative, and at the time his person was all the more esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the Honored Consort came to mourn in person, and only then did people learn he was imperial kin; his stature rose still higher.

sentences.zh: 李周，字通理，邢州內丘人也，唐潞州節度使抱真之後。

translations.literal: Li Zhou, styled Tongli, was a native of Neiqiu in Xing Prefecture, a descendant of Tang's military governor of Lu Prefecture, Li Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou, courtesy name Tongli, came from Neiqiu in Xingzhou and was a descendant of Tang governor Li Baozhen of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融、祖毅、父矩，皆不仕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong, grandfather Yi, and father Ju all held no office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong, grandfather Yi, and father Ju never held office.

sentences.zh: 周年十六，為內丘捕賊將，以任俠自負。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Zhou became bandit-catching commander of Neiqiu and prided himself on chivalrous daring.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he became bandit-catching commander of Neiqiu and prided himself on his chivalry.

sentences.zh: 時河朔群盜充斥，南北交兵，行旅無援者不敢出郡邑。

translations.literal: At that time bandits filled the Hebei region north of the Yellow River; north and south were at war, and travelers without escort did not dare leave their districts and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled the north China plain; with war on every side, travelers without escort dared not leave their towns.

sentences.zh: 有士人盧嶽，家於太原，攜妻子囊橐寓於逆旅，進退無所保，唯與所親相對流涕，周憫之，請援送以歸。

translations.literal: There was a scholar named Lu Yue whose family was at Taiyuan; he carried wife, children, and baggage and lodged at an inn, with no security whether to advance or retreat, weeping face to face only with his kin; Zhou pitied him and asked to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar named Lu Yue, whose family was in Taiyuan, was stranded at an inn with wife, children, and baggage, weeping with his kin and unable to go forward or back; Zhou pitied him and offered to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 行經西山中，有賊夜於林麓間俟之，射盧嶽，中其馬。

translations.literal: Passing through the western hills, bandits waited for them at night in the forested slopes, shot at Lu Yue, and hit his horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the western hills bandits ambushed them at night from the woods, shot at Lu Yue, and struck his horse.

sentences.zh: 周大呼曰：「爾為誰耶？

translations.literal: Zhou shouted loudly: "Who are you?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou shouted, "Who goes there?

sentences.zh: 」賊聞其聲，相謂曰：「李君至此矣。

translations.literal: " Hearing his voice, the bandits said to one another: "Master Li has come here.
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing his voice, the bandits said to one another, "Master Li is here.

sentences.zh: 」即時散走。

translations.literal: " They immediately scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " They scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 嶽全其行裝，至於家。

translations.literal: Yue kept all his traveling gear intact and reached home.
translations.idiomatic: Yue kept his baggage intact and reached home safely.

sentences.zh: 周將辭去，嶽謂周曰：「嶽明歷象，善知人。

translations.literal: As Zhou was about to take leave, Yue said to Zhou: "Yue understands the calendar and celestial signs and is skilled at knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou was leaving, Yue said, "I know the calendar and stars and am skilled at reading men.

sentences.zh: 子有奇表，方頤隆準，眉目疏朗，身長七尺，此乃將相之材也。

translations.literal: You have an extraordinary countenance—square jaw, high nose, clear brows and eyes, seven feet in height; this is the material of generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: You have an extraordinary bearing—square jaw, high nose, clear features, seven feet tall—the makings of a general or minister.

sentences.zh: 河東李氏將有天下，子宜事之，以求富貴。

translations.literal: The Li family of Hedong will possess the realm; you should serve them to seek wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Li of Hedong will win the realm; serve them and you will win wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」周辭以母老而歸。

translations.literal: " Zhou declined on the grounds that his mother was old and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou declined, citing his aged mother, and went home.

sentences.zh: 既而梁將葛從周拔邢、洺，唐武皇麾兵南下，築壘於青山口。

translations.literal: Before long the Liang general Ge Congzhou took Xing and Ming; the Tang Martial Emperor waved his troops south and built fortifications at Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liang general Ge Congzhou took Xing and Ming; the Martial Emperor marched south and built fortifications at Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 周向背莫決，因思盧嶽之言，乃投青山寨將張汙落，武皇賞之，補萬勝黃頭軍使。

translations.literal: Zhou could not decide which side to take; remembering Lu Yue's words, he went over to Zhang Wuluo, commander of the Qingshan stockade; the Martial Emperor rewarded him and appointed him commander of the Wansheng Yellow-Head Army.
translations.idiomatic: Undecided which side to join, Zhou remembered Lu Yue's words and went over to Zhang Wuluo at Qingshan; the Martial Emperor rewarded him and made him commander of the Wansheng Yellow-Head Army.

sentences.zh: 武皇之平雲州，莊宗之戰柏鄉，周皆有功，遷匡霸都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Martial Emperor's pacification of Yun Prefecture and Zhuangzong's battle at Bai Township, Zhou had merit in both and was transferred to commander of the Kuangba Army.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the pacification of Yunzhou and the battle of Baixiang and was made commander of the Kuangba Army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，率兵屯臨河、楊劉，所至與士伍同甘苦。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Wei he led troops garrisoned at Linhe and Yangliu; wherever he went he shared hardship and comfort with the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Zhou garrisoned Linhe and Yangliu and shared every hardship with his men.

sentences.zh: 周尤善守備，一日奔母喪，以他將代之，既出，則其城將陷，莊宗即遣追之，使墨缞從事。

translations.literal: Zhou was especially skilled at defense; one day he rushed off for his mother's funeral and another general replaced him; once he had left the city was about to fall, and Zhuangzong at once sent to recall him and had him take the field in unbleached hemp mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was especially skilled at defense; once he left for his mother's funeral and another general replaced him, the city nearly fell, and Zhuangzong sent for him and had him return in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 會莊宗北征，周與寺人焦彥賓守楊劉城，

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong campaigned north, Zhou and the eunuch Jiao Yanbin defended Yangliu city,
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong marched north, Zhou and the eunuch Jiao Yanbin defended Yangliu,

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·焦彥賓傳》：彥賓字英服，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Jiao Yanbin in the 《Records of the Nine States》: Yanbin, styled Yingfu, was a native of Qingchi in Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: (《Records of the Nine States》, Biography of Jiao Yanbin: Yanbin, courtesy name Yingfu, came from Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，多智略，事武皇，尤所委信。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, full of stratagems; he served the Martial Emperor and was especially entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resourceful in youth, he served the Martial Emperor and was especially trusted.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗即位，遷左監門衛將軍，充四方館使，出護邢州軍。）〉

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was transferred to Left Gate Guard general, made commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, and sent out to protect the Xing Prefecture army.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong acceded he became Left Gate Guard general, commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, and was sent to protect the Xingzhou army.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁將王彥章以數萬眾攻之。

translations.literal: The Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked with tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 周日夜乘城，躬當矢石，使人馳告莊宗，請百里趨程，以紓其難。

translations.literal: Zhou day and night manned the walls, himself facing arrows and stones, and sent men galloping to inform Zhuangzong, asking him to hurry a hundred li to relieve the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou defended the walls day and night in person, under arrow and stone, and sent riders to Zhuangzong begging him to hurry a hundred li to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「李周在內，朕何憂也！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: "With Li Zhou inside, what have I to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "With Li Zhou inside, what have I to fear!

sentences.zh: 」遂日行二舍，不廢畋獵，既至，士眾絕糧三日矣。

translations.literal: " He therefore marched two stages a day without giving up the hunt; when he arrived the troops had been without grain for three days.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched two stages a day without giving up the hunt; when he arrived the garrison had been without food for three days.

sentences.zh: 及攻圍既解，莊宗謂周曰：「微卿九拒之勞，諸公等為梁人所擄矣。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted Zhuangzong said to Zhou: "But for your labor of nine refusals, you gentlemen would have been captured by the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted Zhuangzong told Zhou, "But for your nine days of resistance, you would all be Liang prisoners.

sentences.zh: 」同光中，歷相、蔡二州刺史，及蜀平，授西川節度副使。

translations.literal: " During Tongguang he served successively as prefect of Xiang and Cai Prefectures; when Shu was pacified he was made deputy military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: " During Tongguang he served as prefect of Xiang and Caizhou; when Shu was pacified he was made deputy military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 天成二年春，遷遂州兩使留後，尋正授節旄，未幾，受代歸闕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Tiancheng he was transferred to acting military governor of the two circuits of Sui Prefecture; shortly he received the full commission; before long he was relieved and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second Tiancheng year (927) he became acting governor of Suizhou, soon received the full commission, and before long was relieved and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，出為邠州節度使，會慶州刺史竇廷琬據城拒命，周奉詔討平之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year he was sent out as military governor of Bin Prefecture; the prefect of Qing Prefecture Dou Tingwan held the city and defied orders; Zhou received the edict and suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made military governor of Binzhou; when Qingzhou prefect Dou Tingwan rebelled and held the city, Zhou suppressed him by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 長興、清泰中，歷徐、安、雍、汴四鎮，所至無苛政，人皆樂之。

translations.literal: During Changxing and Qingtai he held the four commands of Xu, An, Yong, and Bian in succession; wherever he went there was no harsh government and the people all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing and Qingtai he held Xu, An, Yong, and Bian in turn; wherever he served his rule was mild and the people were content.

sentences.zh: 高祖有天下，復鎮邠州，累官至檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor possessed the realm, Zhou again garrisoned Bin Prefecture and rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu won the realm, Zhou again governed Binzhou and eventually reached Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及罷鎮赴闕，會少帝幸澶淵，以周累朝耆德，乃命為東京留守。

translations.literal: When he left his command and went to court, it happened that the Young Emperor was visiting Chanyuan; because Zhou was an elder of virtue through successive reigns, he was ordered to be eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his post for court, the Young Emperor was at Chanyuan; considering Zhou a veteran of several reigns, the court made him regent of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，授開封尹。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he was made metropolitan magistrate of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zhou was made metropolitan magistrate of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 及遘疾，夢焚旌旗鎧甲，因自嗟嘆，上章請退，尋卒於官，時年七十四。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he dreamed that banners, flags, and armor were burned; he therefore sighed to himself, memorialized asking to retire, and soon died in office, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he dreamed his banners and armor were burning; he sighed, asked to retire, and soon died in office at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師，陪葬於明宗徽陵之北。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and buried in attendance north of Emperor Mingzong's Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and buried north of Mingzong's Huiling.

sentences.zh: 張從訓，字德恭。

translations.literal: Zhang Congxun, styled Degong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congxun, courtesy name Degong.

sentences.zh: 本姑臧人，其先回鶻別派，隨沙陀徙居雲中，後從唐武皇家於太原，從訓遂為太原人。

translations.literal: Originally a man of Guzang; his forebears were a separate branch of the Uyghurs who followed the Shatuo in moving to Yunzhong; later they followed the Tang Martial Emperor's household to Taiyuan, and Congxun thus became a Taiyuan man.
translations.idiomatic: Originally from Guzang; his ancestors were a Uyghur branch who followed the Shatuo to Yunzhong, then the Martial Emperor's household to Taiyuan, and Congxun became a Taiyuan native.

sentences.zh: 祖君政，雲州長史，識蕃字，通佛理。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junzheng was chief administrator of Yun Prefecture, knew barbarian script, and understood Buddhist principles.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junzheng was chief administrator of Yunzhou, knew barbarian script, and understood Buddhist doctrine.

sentences.zh: 父存信，河東蕃漢馬步軍都指揮使，武皇賜姓名，眷同親嫡，前史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Cunxin was overall commander of barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry in Hedong; the Martial Emperor granted him a surname and personal name and favored him as his own legitimate son; the earlier histories have his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunxin was overall commander of barbarian and Han forces in Hedong; the Martial Emperor gave him the imperial surname and favored him like a son; earlier histories record his biography.

sentences.zh: 天福中，贈太師、中書令，追封趙國公。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從訓讀儒書，精騎射，初為散員大將，天祐中，轄沙陀數百人，屯壺關十餘歲，節度使李嗣昭委遇之。

translations.literal: Congxun read Confucian books and was skilled at mounted archery; he first served as a general of the miscellaneous roster; during Tianyou he commanded several hundred Shatuo men and garrisoned Huguan for more than ten years; the military governor Li Sizhao entrusted him with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun studied the classics and excelled at mounted archery; he first served as a roster general; during Tianyou he commanded several hundred Shatuo troops at Huguan for over ten years and won Li Sizhao's trust.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與梁人相拒於德勝口，征赴軍前，補充先鋒遊奕使，俄轉雲捷指揮使、檢校司空，賜名繼鸞，從諸子之行也。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong faced the Liang at Desheng Ford he was summoned to the front, appointed vanguard roaming commander, shortly transferred to commander of the Yunjie Army and Acting Minister of Works, given the name Jiluan—following the naming of the imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong faced the Liang at Desheng Ford he was summoned to the front as vanguard roaming commander, soon made commander of the Yunjie Army and Honorary Minister of Works, and given the name Jiluan like the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 明宗微時，嘗在存信麾下為都押牙，與從訓有舊，及即位，授石州刺史，復舊姓名。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was still obscure he had once been chief military adjutant under Cunxin and was old friends with Congxun; when he took the throne he appointed him prefect of Shi Prefecture and restored his original surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Mingzong had served under Cunxin as chief adjutant alongside Congxun; on his accession he made Congxun prefect of Shizhou and restored his original name.

sentences.zh: 歷憲、德二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Xian and De Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Xian and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖之鎮太原也，為少帝娶從訓長女為妃。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was stationed at Taiyuan, the Young Emperor was given Congxun's eldest daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was posted at Taiyuan, the Young Emperor married Congxun's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 清泰初授唐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed prefect of Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was appointed prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，高祖舉義，從訓奉唐末帝詔，征赴行在，分領鄉兵，次於團柏谷，兵敗宵遁，潛身民間。

translations.literal: In the third year the High Ancestor raised the righteous cause; Congxun obeyed the Last Tang Emperor's edict, was summoned to the mobile court, led local militia in division, encamped at Tuanbai Valley, was defeated and fled by night, and hid among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Gaozu raised his righteous campaign; Congxun obeyed the Last Emperor's summons, led local militia to Tuanbai Valley, was defeated and fled by night, hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，有詔搜訪，月餘乃出焉，及見戚裏之故，深加軫惻。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered Luoyang there was an edict to search for him; after more than a month he came forth; when he saw his old ties by marriage the court was deeply moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang an edict sought him out; after more than a month he emerged, and on seeing his old ties by marriage the court was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 尋授絳州刺史、檢校太保，在任數年，天福中，卒於官，年五十二。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made prefect of Jiang Prefecture and Acting Grand Guardian; he held office several years; during Tianfu he died in office, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Jiangzhou and Honorary Grand Guardian; after several years in office he died during Tianfu at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 少帝以後父之故，超贈太尉。

translations.literal: Because he was the Young Emperor's father-in-law, he was posthumously promoted beyond precedent to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: As the Young Emperor's father-in-law, he was posthumously promoted to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 弟從恩仕皇朝，為右金吾衛上將軍，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Cong'en served the imperial court as senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Cong'en served the dynasty as senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and died in office.

sentences.zh: 始繼忠母楊氏善治產，平生積財巨萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning Jizhong's mother the Lady Yang was skilled at managing property and in her lifetime amassed wealth of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong's mother Lady Yang was skilled at managing wealth and amassed a fortune in her lifetime.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，楊已終，繼忠舉族家於晉陽。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan, Yang had already died; Jizhong moved his whole clan's household to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his campaign at Taiyuan, Yang had already died, and Jizhong moved his clan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 時以諸軍方困，契丹援兵又至，高祖乃使人就其第，疏其復壁，取其舊積，所獲金銀紈素甚廣，至於巾屨瑣屑之物，無不取足。

translations.literal: At that time because the various armies were in distress and Khitan relief troops had also arrived, the High Ancestor sent men to his residence, broke through the layered walls, and took his old stores; the gold, silver, and silk obtained were very extensive, and even down to towels, shoes, and trifling items nothing was left ungathered in full.
translations.idiomatic: With the armies in distress and Khitan reinforcements arriving, Gaozu sent men to his house, broke through the walls, and seized his hoard—gold, silver, silk in vast quantities, even towels and shoes, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 高祖既濟大事，感而奇之，故車駕入洛，繼忠雖有舊恙，連領大郡，皆楊氏之力也。

translations.literal: After the High Ancestor had accomplished the great affair he was moved and regarded it as extraordinary; therefore when the imperial carriage entered Luoyang, although Jizhong had an old ailment, he was repeatedly given large commands—all through the Lady Yang's power.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu succeeded he was moved by the windfall; when the court entered Luoyang, Jizhong—though in poor health—was given one large command after another, all thanks to Lady Yang's hoard.

sentences.zh: 李頃，陳州項城人，即河陽節度使、兼侍中罕之子也。

translations.literal: Li Qing was a native of Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture, the son of the military governor of Heyang and concurrent Palace Attendant Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing came from Xiangcheng in Chenzhou and was the son of Heyang military governor and Palace Attendant Li Han.

sentences.zh: 罕之，《梁書》有傳。

translations.literal: Han has a biography in the 《Book of Liang》.
translations.idiomatic: Han has a biography in the 《Book of Liang》.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，罕之與河南張全義為仇，交相攻擊，罕之兵敗，北投太原，武皇以澤州處之，罕之將赴任，留頃為質焉。

translations.literal: In Guangqi of Tang, Han and Zhang Quanyi of Henan were enemies and attacked each other in turn; Han's army was defeated and he fled north to submit to Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor settled him at Ze Prefecture; as Han was about to take up his post he left Qing as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Guangqi (888–904) Han feuded with Zhang Quanyi of Henan; defeated, he fled north to Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor gave him Zezhou, and as Han departed for his post he left Qing as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗未弱冠，因與頃遊處，甚相昵狎。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong had not yet reached twenty; he therefore associated with Qing in his travels and was very intimate and familiar with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was not yet twenty and spent much time with Qing; the two were very close.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，罕之自澤州襲據潞州，送款於梁，武皇以頃父叛，將殺之，莊宗密與駿騎，使逃出境，頃遂奔河南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Han launched a surprise attack from Ze Prefecture and seized Luzhou, and sent submission to Liang; the Martial Emperor, because Qing's father had rebelled, was about to kill him; Zhuangzong secretly gave him swift horses and had him flee beyond the border; Qing then fled to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangqi (888) Han seized Luzhou from Zezhou and submitted to Liang; the Martial Emperor meant to kill Qing because his father had rebelled, but Zhuangzong secretly gave him fast horses to escape, and Qing fled to Henan.

sentences.zh: 梁祖以其父子歸己，委遇甚厚。

translations.literal: The Liang founder regarded father and son as having come over to him and entrusted and favored them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder treated father and son as his own men and favored them generously.

sentences.zh: 天復中，梁祖自鳳翔送唐昭宗歸長安，留軍萬人，命侄友倫與頃總之，以宿衛為名。

translations.literal: During Tianfu the Liang founder escorted Tang Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang back to Chang'an, left ten thousand troops, and ordered his nephew Youlun and Qing to command them jointly, in the name of palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu (901–904) the Liang founder escorted Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang to Chang'an, left ten thousand troops, and put his nephew Youlun and Qing jointly in command as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖逼禪，累掌禁兵，倚為肘腋。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder forced the abdication, Qing repeatedly held command of the forbidden troops and was relied on as a close aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder forced the abdication, Qing repeatedly commanded the palace guards and was relied on as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 庶人友珪立，授頃檢校尚書右僕射、右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: When the commoner Yougui took the throne, Qing was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui took the throne, Qing was made Honorary Right Vice Director and commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝之誅友珪，頃預其謀，尋歷隨州刺史，復為右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: When the Last Liang Emperor executed Yougui, Qing took part in the plot; shortly he served as prefect of Sui Prefecture and again became commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army.
translations.idiomatic: Qing took part in the Last Liang Emperor's plot to kill Yougui; he later served as prefect of Suizhou and again commanded the Right Forest of Feathers Army.

sentences.zh: 同光初，莊宗入汴，召頃見之，莊宗忻然，授衛州刺史，加光祿大夫、檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang Zhuangzong entered Bian; he summoned Qing to see him; Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him prefect of Wei Prefecture, adding Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang Zhuangzong entered Bian and summoned Qing; pleased to see him, he made him prefect of Weizhou and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，授衍州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Mingzong reign he was appointed prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 長興中，檢校太傅、右神武統軍。

translations.literal: During Changxing he was Acting Grand Tutor and commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he was Honorary Grand Tutor and commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之二年，加特進、檢校太尉、右領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of the High Ancestor's accession he was given the extraordinary rank of Grand Master, Acting Grand Commandant, and senior general of the Right Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Gaozu's reign he was made Grand Master, Honorary Grand Commandant, and senior general of the Right Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，進封開國伯。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to enfeoffment as Earl with a state-founding fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was enfeoffed as Earl.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷左領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to senior general of the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋以病卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died of illness, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness at seventy.

sentences.zh: 制贈太師。

translations.literal: By decree he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 頃性溫雅，不暴虐，凡刺郡統眾，頗有畏愛，及卒，人甚惜之。

translations.literal: Qing's nature was mild and refined, not violent or cruel; whenever he governed a prefecture or commanded troops the people both feared and loved him; when he died people deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was mild and never cruel; in every command he won both respect and affection, and people deeply mourned him when he died.

sentences.zh: 子彥弼，在太原日，因頃走歸梁朝，武皇怒，下蠶室加熏腐之刑，後籍於內侍省，卒焉。

translations.literal: His son Yanbi, while at Taiyuan, because Qing had fled back to the Liang court, the Martial Emperor was angry and sent him to the silkworm chamber to undergo castration by fumigation; later he was registered in the Directorate of Palace Attendants and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanbi, left behind at Taiyuan when Qing fled to Liang, was castrated by the Martial Emperor in anger and later entered palace service, where he died.

sentences.zh: 光輔有弟數人，光貞歷義、乾二州刺史，入為諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Guangfu had several younger brothers; Guangzhen served successively as prefect of Yi and Qian Prefectures and entered court as a general of the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu had several younger brothers: Guangzhen served as prefect of Yi and Qianzhou and became a guard general at court.

sentences.zh: 光遜繼為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangxun succeeded him as prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxun succeeded him as prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 光贊任青州行軍司馬，及楊光遠叛滅，貶商州司馬，會赦征還，尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Guangzan served as campaigning deputy of Qing Prefecture; when Yang Guangyuan rebelled and was destroyed he was demoted to deputy of Shang Prefecture; when an amnesty was proclaimed he was summoned back and soon died at home.
